quizzes.title: JavaScript & TypeScript Engineering Assessment
quizzes.description: Evaluates production-grade TypeScript idioms, async concurrency, type narrowing, and execution context.

questions.question: In the JavaScript event loop, in what order will 'Promise.resolve().then(cb)', 'setTimeout(cb, 0)', and synchronous code execute?
options: setTimeout callback -> Promise microtask -> Synchronous code
Synchronous code -> Promise microtask -> setTimeout macrotask
Synchronous code -> setTimeout macrotask -> Promise microtask
Promise microtask -> Synchronous code -> setTimeout macrotask
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs to completion on the call stack, after which the microtask queue (Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask) is completely drained before macrotasks (setTimeout, setInterval) execute.

questions.question: How does TypeScript enforce exhaustiveness checking in a discriminated union switch statement?
options: By annotating the default branch with variable assignment to 'never'
By decorating the function with @exhaustive
By declaring all switch cases inside a try...catch block
By casting the input to 'unknown' before checking
questions.explanation: Assigning the unmatched switch variable to a variable of type 'never' in the default branch causes TypeScript to throw a compile-time type error if any union member was unhandled.

questions.question: Which of the following will properly deep clone an object containing nested objects and arrays without losing Date objects or circular references?
options: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj))
Object.assign({}, obj)
structuredClone(obj)
questions.explanation: The native structuredClone() API performs a structured clone algorithm supporting Dates, Sets, Maps, and cyclical references, unlike JSON serialization.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Promise.all and Promise.allSettled?
options: Promise.all runs sequentially, whereas Promise.allSettled runs in parallel
Promise.all rejects immediately upon the first rejection, whereas Promise.allSettled waits for all promises to resolve or reject
Promise.all returns an array of status objects, whereas Promise.allSettled returns only raw values
Promise.allSettled is deprecated in modern Node.js runtimes
questions.explanation: Promise.all fast-fails when any promise rejects. Promise.allSettled waits for every promise to settle and provides an array describing the outcome of each.

questions.question: In TypeScript, what is the key benefit of using 'unknown' over 'any'?
options: 'unknown' disables all type checking just like 'any'
'unknown' requires type narrowing or type assertion before operations can be safely performed on the value
'unknown' can only represent primitive types
'unknown' is only valid in server-side Next.js code
questions.explanation: 'unknown' is the type-safe counterpart of 'any'. You cannot access arbitrary properties or invoke methods on an 'unknown' value without narrowing its type first.

quizzes.title: Relational Database Design & Indexing
quizzes.description: Tests knowledge of B-Tree indexing rules, ACID isolation, foreign key constraints, and query plan performance.

questions.question: Given a composite B-Tree index on (department_id, graduation_year, cgpa), which query will NOT be able to utilize this index efficiently?
options: WHERE department_id = 'CSE' AND graduation_year = 2026
WHERE department_id = 'CSE'
WHERE graduation_year = 2026 AND cgpa > 8.0
WHERE department_id = 'CSE' AND graduation_year = 2026 AND cgpa > 8.0
questions.explanation: B-Tree composite indexes require queries to filter on the leading columns (leftmost prefix). A query filtering only on 'graduation_year' skips 'department_id' and cannot use the index tree traversal efficiently.

questions.question: In ACID transaction guarantees, which isolation level prevents Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads, but allows Phantom Reads in standard ANSI SQL?
options: Read Uncommitted
Read Committed
Repeatable Read
Serializable
questions.explanation: Repeatable Read ensures that any row read during a transaction cannot be modified by another transaction. In traditional ANSI SQL, new rows matching a range query (phantom reads) could still appear unless Serializable is used.

questions.question: Why should you avoid placing an index on a low-cardinality boolean column like 'is_active' in a 1,000,000-row table?
options: Boolean indexes are not supported in modern relational databases
The query optimizer will usually favor a sequential scan because half the rows match anyway
Boolean indexes corrupt database transaction logs
Boolean values cannot be balanced in a B-Tree node
questions.explanation: When a column has low selectivity (cardinality), the query planner calculates that traversing index pages plus random heap lookups is slower than a sequential block scan.

questions.question: What is the key criterion for a database table to satisfy Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)?
options: It must contain no composite primary keys
For every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey
It must store all array relationships in JSONB columns
It must have exactly one foreign key per table
questions.explanation: BCNF is a stricter version of 3NF where every determinant (left side of any non-trivial functional dependency) must be a superkey of the relation.

questions.question: What is connection pool starvation in database systems?
options: When memory on the database server runs out due to large temp tables
When all available pool connections are held by active or slow queries, causing new requests to queue or timeout
When the database drops network connections after idle timeout
When replication lag prevents secondary replicas from accepting read queries
questions.explanation: Connection starvation happens when web workers acquire database connections and hold them during slow external API calls or unindexed queries, blocking other HTTP requests from obtaining a connection.

quizzes.title: Modern React & Frontend Architecture
quizzes.description: Evaluates React 19 / Next.js App Router patterns, hooks lifecycle, reconciliation, and Core Web Vitals.

questions.question: Why is using array index as a 'key' prop considered an anti-pattern when rendering dynamic lists in React?
options: It causes compile errors in React 19
Reordering or deleting items causes React to misidentify component identities, leading to incorrect state retention and DOM churn
Array indices cannot be cast to strings in JSX
It disables React concurrent memoization completely
questions.explanation: Keys tell React which item is which across renders. When using indices, deleting or reordering shifts index positions, causing React to associate old component instance states with new data items.

questions.question: In Next.js App Router, which file convention defines a fallback UI rendered automatically via React Suspense while route segments load?
options: error.tsx
loading.tsx
skeleton.tsx
page.loading.tsx
questions.explanation: Next.js automatically wraps page components in a React <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}> boundary when a loading.tsx file exists in the route segment folder.

questions.question: How do you avoid race conditions when fetching data inside a client component useEffect hook without an external library?
options: Set the dependency array to [Date.now()]
Use a boolean 'ignore' / 'cancelled' flag in the effect cleanup function to disregard out-of-order resolved promises
Wrap the fetch call in a synchronous while-loop
Declare the effect callback as 'async () => {}'
questions.explanation: By setting `let cancelled = false; return () => { cancelled = true; }`, if inputs change before the previous network call finishes, the previous promise result is discarded safely.

questions.question: In modern CSS Flexbox, why might text truncation ('truncate' / 'text-overflow: ellipsis') fail inside a flex child?
options: Flex children default to 'min-width: auto', which prevents shrinking below content size unless 'min-width: 0' is applied
Ellipsis is only supported in grid layouts
Flex containers cannot have text nodes
The browser requires 'display: inline-flex' for truncation
questions.explanation: By default, flex children have `min-width: auto`, which forbids the child from shrinking smaller than its intrinsic content width. Setting `min-width: 0` allows flex items to shrink and trigger text truncation.

questions.question: Which Core Web Vital measures the time from when the user initiates navigation to when the largest image or text block within the viewport is rendered?
options: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
Time to First Byte (TTFB)
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures perceived loading speed and marks the point in the page load timeline when the primary content has likely loaded.

quizzes.title: Python, Pandas & Machine Learning Foundations
quizzes.description: Tests vectorization, EDA, model evaluation metrics, and general machine learning engineering practices.

questions.question: Why is vectorized computation in NumPy and Pandas significantly faster than native Python for-loops over arrays?
options: Vectorized functions execute compiled C/Fortran code in contiguous memory blocks with SIMD hardware instructions and avoid Python GIL overhead per element
NumPy automatically uploads data to an external cloud cluster
Python for-loops convert every number to a string internally
Vectorized code runs exclusively on GPUs
questions.explanation: NumPy arrays are stored in contiguous C memory buffers and vectorized operations execute compiled machine code using CPU SIMD instructions, avoiding dynamic Python type-checking and interpreter overhead on each iteration.

questions.question: In an imbalanced binary fraud detection problem where positive fraud cases are only 0.2% of the dataset, why is standard Accuracy a deceptive metric?
options: Accuracy cannot be calculated on float values
A naive dummy classifier predicting 'Not Fraud' 100% of the time achieves 99.8% accuracy while failing to detect a single fraudulent case
Accuracy requires equal numbers of features and rows
Scikit-learn disallows accuracy on binary targets
questions.explanation: With extreme class imbalance, a model that classifies everything as the majority class has high accuracy but zero recall. Precision-Recall AUC or F1-Score are far more informative.

questions.question: What does it indicate if the training loss continues to decrease steadily while validation loss starts increasing after epoch 12?
options: The model is underfitting the training distribution
The model is overfitting to noise in the training set and losing generalization power
The learning rate is too low
The dataset has zero bias
questions.explanation: Divergence between decreasing training loss and increasing validation loss is the canonical signature of overfitting. Early stopping should halt training at this inflection point.

questions.question: Why should feature scaling parameters (e.g. mean and standard deviation in StandardScaler) be fit ONLY on the training split, and not on the entire dataset?
options: To avoid data leakage from the test set into the model training pipeline
Because test sets cannot contain negative values
Because StandardScaler only accepts 100 rows at a time
To allow the test set to normalize itself independently
questions.explanation: Fitting scalers or imputers on the full dataset leaks test set statistics into the training phase, giving an unrealistically optimistic estimate of true out-of-sample performance.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between standard K-Fold and Stratified K-Fold cross-validation?
options: Stratified K-Fold ensures each fold maintains the same percentage of target class labels as the complete dataset
Stratified K-Fold works only on continuous regression targets
Standard K-Fold is deterministic, while Stratified is random
Stratified K-Fold trains on all folds at the same time
questions.explanation: Stratification preserves class proportions across all cross-validation folds, which is vital for preventing folds with missing or skewed representation of minority classes.
